intent: Split the 302-line transcribe_fw.py into a progress-reporting module and the transcription entry point, both under the 250-line cap, moving every definition verbatim.
scope: transcribe_fw.py 302 -> 236 (argument parsing, model loading, diarized output, main)
Re-pointed the module under test for the two progress functions
changes: Extracted _run_progress_loop and _format_progress_line into _transcribe_progress.py, together with the two constants only they use (_PROGRESS_THROTTLE_SEC, _SECONDS_PER_DAY) and the hhmmss import they need.
transcribe_fw.py imports _run_progress_loop by name and no longer imports time, which only the progress code used.

The progress tests now patch _transcribe_progress - including its sys.stderr and time references, which is where the loop resolves them. _resolve_device_and_compute stayed in transcribe_fw, so its test was left pointing there.
_transcribe_progress.py was given the executable bit to match the repo convention for a file carrying a shebang.

verification.evidence: IDENTICAL: all 8 top-level definitions moved verbatim. Re-run after ruff reordered the imports, and still identical.

verification.command: AST scan for names used but not bound in each module
verification.evidence: Both modules report no unbound names, confirming the two constants and the hhmmss import travelled with the code that uses them.
32 passed - the same count as before the split. _transcribe_progress.py: 43 statements, 16 branches, 100%. transcribe_fw.py: 95 statements, 16 branches, 100%.

Help prints the full usage; the missing-dependency path logs 'faster-whisper is not installed in this environment.' and returns exit 2, the code transcribe.sh branches on. Only a real run proves the sibling imports still resolve after a split.
275 passed, unchanged from before the split.
33 files over cap, down from 34. The two modules are 236 and 91 lines.

risks: transcribe_fw.py at 236 lines has only 14 lines of headroom under the cap. A further split is available if it grows: _parse_args and _load_whisper_model are an obvious next seam.

The progress module is imported by transcribe_fw by bare name, which resolves because they are siblings on sys.path[0]. That is the existing convention for this directory, shared with _transcribe_diarize, _transcribe_model and _transcribe_output, and the real run confirms it.
rollback: git revert the commit; transcribe_fw.py returns to its 302-line form and _transcribe_progress.py disappears.
After rollback, confirm python3 transcribe_fw.py /nonexistent.wav still returns 2 and pytest linux_configuration/tests/ reports 275 passed.
